speaker: Mr Yip Hon Weng
text: asked the Prime Minister whether the Public Service Division can share what are the plans (i) to set up more ServiceSG centres across Singapore and to involve more partnering agencies in the initiative and (ii) to require that at the same time for Ministries and agencies to set aside physical counters for seniors requiring assistance to assess public services.

speaker: The Minister for Education (Mr Chan Chun Sing) (for the Prime Minister)
text: We have put in place schemes and initiatives to bridge the digital divide, by enabling digital access and accessibility, and upskilling citizens on digital skills and knowledge.

speaker: The Minister for Education (Mr Chan Chun Sing) (for the Prime Minister)
text: We have significantly expanded the number of ServiceSG Centres to better serve the community.

speaker: The Minister for Education (Mr Chan Chun Sing) (for the Prime Minister)
text: We will continue to expand the network of centres to prioritise areas with higher demand and concentration of citizens, particularly seniors, who require support with multiple digital transactions.

speaker: The Minister for Education (Mr Chan Chun Sing) (for the Prime Minister)
text: Presently, our agencies with physical service centres primarily offer in-person assistance on an appointment-only basis.

speaker: The Minister for Education (Mr Chan Chun Sing) (for the Prime Minister)
text: This approach allows citizens to schedule visits at their convenience for transactions that cannot be completed online, thereby reducing the frustration of long queues or wait times.

speaker: The Minister for Education (Mr Chan Chun Sing) (for the Prime Minister)
text: While agencies encourage citizens to make appointments for face-to-face consultations, they do exercise discretion in assisting less digitally savvy and vulnerable individuals who walk in without making appointments.

speaker: The Minister for Education (Mr Chan Chun Sing) (for the Prime Minister)
text: Trained service ambassadors are also present at these service centres to assist less digitally literate individuals in triaging their needs and completing their transactions.

speaker: Mr Yip Hon Weng (Yio Chu Kang)
text: I also thank him for his reply to my cut on service delivery during yesterday's Prime Minister's Office (PMO) Committee of Supply debate.

speaker: Mr Yip Hon Weng (Yio Chu Kang)
text: Good to hear that we are expanding more ServiceSG Centres across Singapore – and I hope to get one in Ang Mo Kio and also in Yio Chu Kang.

speaker: Mr Yip Hon Weng (Yio Chu Kang)
text: First, are there plans to increase the availability of multilingual support at the ServiceSG Centres to serve Singapore's diverse population?

speaker: Mr Yip Hon Weng (Yio Chu Kang)
text: Second, are there plans by the Public Service to ensure that ServiceSG Centres do not simply duplicate existing services offered by individual Ministries and agencies, but rather, take the opportunity of co-location to streamline services?

speaker: Mr Yip Hon Weng (Yio Chu Kang)
text: This could mean, perhaps, rewiring certain protocols and processes, reduce duplication and perhaps, find new ways of doing things.

speaker: Mr Chan Chun Sing
text: First, yes, we have received Mr Yip Hon Weng's Yip Chu Kang and Ang Mo Kio request and we are processing it now.
